decisions.reason: Only column whose name matches the target convention (name_matches_target_convention true) and it is discrete with 2 values; the other low-cardinality categoricals (brew_preference, geological_era, instrument, species, region) are named like features and the numeric columns have thousands of distinct values, so they are measures rather than classes.
alternatives_considered: brew_preference - 2 classes but a named feature (Espresso/Latte), not a task label
geological_era / weather_pattern / instrument / species / region - low-cardinality categorical predictors, not labels
aptitude_score / performance_score - near-continuous measures (15,148 and 24,418 distinct values)

decisions.choice: keep outliers; drop rows with no label; rarest class: keep; no columns excluded
decisions.reason: No column is an identifier or timestamp: structure.json examined all 15 features and the closest grouping candidate (mineral_type, 1,944.5 rows/value, lift 5.2) is itself a model feature, so grouping on it would cut folds through the signal. 3 rows have no label and are dropped (a missing label can be neither imputed nor scored). Missing feature values are sparse (50 cells, 0.02%) and look at random, so the pipeline's per-fold median/mode imputation is enough. The rare class 'yes' is a real, well-supported class (7,464 rows, no duplicates, no contradictions, lift 2.34), so it is kept. Numeric extremes are kept: they are plausible measurements and not the rare-class signal, so an IQR fence would only delete data.
alternatives_considered: drop_columns for mineral_type/region as entity keys - rejected: is_in_feature_set is true for every candidate, so they are predictors, not entities
IQR outlier filtering - rejected: removes genuine measurements on a mild 3.17:1 imbalance, where the minority rows are the ones most likely to be extreme
drop_duplicated_rows for the rare class - rejected: effective_unique_rows equals n_rows (no duplication) and contradicted_rows is 0

decisions.reason: gradient_boosting: Top of the f1_macro shortlist (screen mean 0.7665 +/- 0.0053) and a natural fit for a 31k-row, 82-wide tabular frame; boosting fits small staircases to residuals, which reaches the smooth, low-order boundary this mix of 7 numeric and 8 one-hot columns suggests. Grid was kept to 8 combinations because the axis is expensive and each unit of n_estimators re-grows the whole ensemble. logistic_regression: Second on the f1_macro screen (0.7649 +/- 0.0054) and the only linear-in-the-log-odds family in the registry, so the comparison against the tree boundary is maximally informative. One-hot encoding gives each category its own signed coefficient, which is readable. C spans two orders of magnitude around the default; class_weight is searched because the label is 3.17:1 and rebalancing may or may not help once the metric already weights classes equally.
alternatives_considered: random_forest - shortlisted on shape but shares gradient_boosting's axis-aligned bias, so the pair would reach one boundary shape twice
svm - below the f1_macro floor (0.7587); also costs more than linearly in rows
decision_tree / knn / naive_bayes - clearly behind on the screen
svm - within the accuracy shortlist but below on macro-F1 and more expensive on rows; a kernel boundary is less interpretable here
knn - scaling-dependent and weaker (0.7469); 82 one-hot columns dilute its distance
naive_bayes - weakest family (0.6631) and its per-column-independence assumption is violated by correlated one-hot columns

stopping.gradient_boosting: n_estimators (100-300) and learning_rate caps; no early stopping
stopping.logistic_regression: solver max_iter=2000, tol 1e-4; cap not reached

decisions.reason: gradient_boosting: not required - trees split on order, so the units cannot move a split logistic_regression: generally recommended and close to required - one shared L2 penalty, so unscaled units dominate the coefficients and slow the solver
alternatives_considered: gradient_boosting with scale=True - the registry's stated preference for this family is in reference.md section 3
logistic_regression with scale=False - the registry's stated preference for this family is in reference.md section 3

decisions.reason: structure.json gives no evidence of repeated entities or time ordering: every grouping candidate is a model feature (is_in_feature_set true) and there are no time candidates, so rows are independent and a stratified split is correct. The rare class holds 7,464 of 31,109 rows, so a 20% holdout validates about 1,493 'yes' rows - a single flipped rare row moves recall by ~0.07%, so one estimate is already stable and k-fold would multiply fitting cost for little gain. test_size is unused because a labelled test file was supplied.
alternatives_considered: stratified_kfold (5-fold) - rejected: the rare class is well populated, so the extra stability does not justify 5x the fitting time
grouped_holdout on mineral_type - rejected: it is a predictor (is_in_feature_set true), and grouping on it cuts folds through the signal
temporal - rejected: no time column exists

decisions.reason: The search optimises the same metric the report leads with, f1_macro, so selection and reporting share one ruler; on a 3.17:1 label accuracy would reward the majority and this is a case where both classes carry equal weight.
alternatives_considered: accuracy as the tuning metric - rejected: dominated by the 76% majority class
final_fit_scope 'train' - rejected: throws away the validation rows for no reason under a holdout
final_fit_scope 'train+validation' - equivalent to 'pool' here; 'pool' names the intent (everything but the test) directly

decisions.reason: The task is a binary label with no stated asymmetry between a false positive and a false negative, so both classes matter equally; the classes are imbalanced 3.17:1 (23,645 'no' vs 7,464 'yes'), so a metric that weights the majority would flatter a model that ignores 'yes'. Macro-F1 averages recall and precision over both classes equally, it is the metric the search optimised, and the ~1,493 rare rows in the validation block make it stable to estimate.
alternatives_considered: accuracy - At a 76% majority floor accuracy stays high even when the minority is missed.

decisions.decision: what the final model is fitted on
decisions.reason: Under a holdout the validation block was used only to select hyperparameters, so refitting on the whole non-test pool (train + validation, 31,109 rows) is the standard choice; the external test file stays untouched by selection, and no label is discarded from the final fit.
alternatives_considered: train - the scopes differ in how much data the final fit sees and, for 'pool', in whether the test estimate is still untouched by selection
train+validation - the scopes differ in how much data the final fit sees and, for 'pool', in whether the test estimate is still untouched by selection
